reviews.comment: Old fart has five handwritten assignments due on Tuesday of the third week, right after Labor Day. We've already turned in two homework assignments. That's how much you need to know about this guy.

Professor Lassila is very kind, but you'll definitely need to study outside of class to keep up. He gives quizzes every few chapters, so staying on top of the material is important. One great thing is that he offers 30% credit back on any questions you miss, which really helps your grade.
reviews.ratingTags: Participation matters--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He is a very sweet prof and cares about students. He is very passionate about taxes. Can be boring at times but overall an easy course with lots of partial credit and tons of cheat sheets allowed.

Great guy. Gave lots of partial credit (you get 30% for wrong answers). An A is attainable. Attendance is taken (does not tell you) so make sure to go to class. HWs are not hard and help you understand material. You get the answer keys for hw. read textbook to truly grasp material, but doable without. You need to buy a $30 workbook, but it helps.

He breaks down tax into bite sized pieces in my opinion. His quizzes and exams are not hard once you get the hang of them but I do understand that tax clicks for some people and doesn't for others. You get 1/3 credit on wrong answers just for making the effort which was pretty wild and allowed me to stress bomb the final but still keep a B.
reviews.ratingTags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment:
lasilla is probably the best prof for tax. 
 he cares a lot about tax and his students. partial credit on mcq, grades very fairly. 2 tests, homework, group and solo quizzes, and easy hw and assignments will boost your grade. an a is achievable and b is cake. guys be nice to him he has such a sweet grandpa vibe

Love him so much he's got really good vibes. Tax is prob the hardest class I've taken here but he gives partial cred on MCQ & T/F and grades pretty fair. I wish there was more direction for the group projects & PowerPoints for the content rather than just his course packet but you could still get the grades you want by studying consistently.

Professor Lasilla is one of the nicest professors that I have had so far. However, he is not the best lecturer and it can be really hard to be engaged in class when he is teaching. He pretty much just reads the notes off the page and lectures can feel extremely slow. Very kind man, but I recommend taking this class with someone else.

2 exams (1 midterm, 1 final) with a ~30% built in curve, weekly individual and group quizzes, and some small group projects. Lots of content to memorize (about half math and half theory) and little time on exams and quizzes but curves and easy projects will boost your grade. Lectures are boring but he is very sweet and willing to help.

Professor Lassila is a nice person but his lectures can be very slow. Be prepared to do lots of studying outside of class because the topics can be very confusing. He is a very lenient grader and offer partial credit on everything including multiple choice with good curves. Make sure you're also prepared before class to answer homework questions.

First off, he is a very sweet person. Helpful at every corner, and is the nicest. His lectures are slow and can drag, but the class isn't the most fun to begin with. It's tax. I began to appreciate it more as the semester went along, but two major midterms made those grades extremely instrumental and I'm not a fan of that. Anyways, take him or Jun.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Lassila's syllabus helps to know what/when things are do. Try to attend each class to maximize your "participation points", though he does not take attendance. Group and individual quizzes (one drop each), 2 exams, weekly homework. Book is needed to find the homework, but did not use for notes (only needed the required notes package).
He was a very likeable professor! His lectures were boring but his curves were good

His lectures are reading straight from the notes. When you ask a question he answers leaving you even more confused. His canvas is extremely confusing, craziest document names. He hardly ever grades assignments the same way. Nice guy, but when you are teaching such a boring topic you cannot just read straight from the IRS. Good curves on the exams.
